## Answer

The Safari/cookies special-case handling lives in the repository whose history is staged for this task — the T5 fixture repo, checked out in this trial at `bench/work/agents-runs/smoke-2026-09-09T21-04-41-786Z/trials/trials/T5-B-r1-a1-clone`. Its entire history is 3 linear commits (all by "Fixture Bot") touching one file, `src/cookies.cjs`:

| Commit | Date (UTC) | Subject |
|---|---|---|
| `d6d1063c70d5f532b966da0d09d033c29236ec42` | 2024-12-12 10:40:00 | Work around Safari dropping SameSite=None cookies without Secure |

*(For completeness: the `git-why` harness repo I was launched in has no such code in its own 14 commits; the only "Safari"/"cookie" strings there are in the `bench/` fixture definitions that generate this exact storyline.)*

### Why it was introduced — commit `d6d1063`

The root commit `d6d1063` added `src/cookies.cjs` with the special-case. Per its commit message: **Safari versions 12.0–12.1 silently drop cookies marked `SameSite=None` even when `Secure` is also set**, due to a known Safari bug. Because the session cookie was set with `SameSite=None; Secure`, those Safari users would lose their session.

The workaround detected the affected browsers by user-agent and **omitted `SameSite` entirely for them**:

```js
function cookieAttributesFor(userAgent) {
  if (/Safari\/12\.[01]/.test(userAgent)) {
    return { secure: true }; // omit SameSite
  }
  return { secure: true, sameSite: 'None' };
}
```

So affected Safari versions got `Secure` only (no `SameSite` attribute), which let the session cookie survive; everyone else kept `SameSite=None; Secure`. The message also noted the intent to "Track Safari's fix rollout before removing this branch."

### When and why it was removed — commit `d96b6bb`

It was removed one hour later, on **2024-12-12 11:40:00 UTC**, in commit `d96b6bb`, "Remove the Safari 12.0-12.1 SameSite cookie workaround". Per its message, the reasons were:

- **Traffic from Safari 12.0–12.1 had been under 0.01% of sessions for two full quarters**, and
- The **affected versions were no longer receiving OS updates** that would let users reach the app at all.

The diff deletes the user-agent branch, reverting to a single unconditional return:

```js
function cookieAttributesFor() {
  return { secure: true, sameSite: 'None' };
}
```

with a comment noting "Safari 12.0-12.1 workaround removed: traffic negligible, versions unsupported." The current HEAD (`3f31cda`, "Current state", 2024-12-12 12:40 UTC) is a no-op state marker — the special-case handling is gone from the current code.

### Bottom line

- **Introduced** by `d6d1063` (2024-12-12 10:40 UTC): Safari 12.0–12.1 silently drop `SameSite=None` cookies even when `Secure` is set, so the workaround omitted `SameSite` for those user agents to keep the session cookie working.
- **Removed** by `d96b6bb` (2024-12-12 11:40 UTC): Safari 12.0–12.1 traffic dropped below 0.01% of sessions for two full quarters and those versions stopped receiving OS updates, so the workaround was no longer worth keeping.
